label: design:t256-0
title: No cold-half engine-rate design clears the T=256 bar. The ea4 cold half is bound by HBM and fixed cost, not by its K-step. Best cold-side stack is about -15..-30 us, so headline 0.
mechanism:
VERDICT: no engine change to the cold half can take >= 45 us off verify_32, so headline_gain_pct is 0. Five reasons:

(1) HBM bounds the cold half, not the K-step. At T=256 the cold half holds 18 / 16 / 17 cold experts at the gate's p10 / p50 / p90 draws (109 / 100 / 106 routes), almost all of them one-tile single passes.
- After L3/L4, Engine A's K-step takes 1,740.6 cycles per 65,536-weight record per SM at T=8 one-tile (eac_s4_l4_t8, 37.6 el/clk/SM) and 2,045.7 at T=16 (32.0).
- The HBM ring supplies 4.37 TB/s / 132 SMs / 0.5625 B per el = 33.2 el/clk/SM at the judge's 1,769 MHz.
- The judge's cold-half anatomies (9 decode runs, serial H-16) run at 2.86-3.26 TB/s and fit 27.4 + 7.34 k_c us. 7.34 us per pass is 88% of the ring ceiling (6.48 us); the consumer alone needs 5.72 us.
- Dequant, LSU, LDSM and MEMBAR do not set the cold stream:
  - P3b: no pipe is above 56% of SM-active, and every LDS/LDSM is at 1.000x ideal.
  - Deleting all scale work (eac sc0, an illegal ceiling) gives only x1.12 over L4.
  - More consumer warpgroups give <= +3%.
- At p50, HBM sets 117 us of the stream. A fixed term sets the other 27.4 us: the empty K1+K2 chain, two stream-K fix-up rounds (D = +4.35 / +4.90 us), build_map at R=2048 twice, two ring fills, and the K1 -> K2 PDL hand-off.

(2) The ceiling is below the bar. At p50 the cold bytes are 16 x 28.31 MB = 453 MB, which takes 103.7 us at the ring ceiling. A perfect cold engine (100% of the ring, zero fixed cost) would remove 41 us from today's 144.8 us. That is short of 45 us, and no engine can reach it.

(3) The fork does not change this.
- The T=256 fork adds the two halves' SM time:
  - On the judge, H-16f / H-16 is x1.049 / 1.032 / 1.066, which saves only 9.6-21 us.
  - On the node (m03c E3), cold K1 takes all 264 CTA slots for 152.7 us (150.8 serial), the hot w13 waits until 136.7 us (median), and the hot path is blocked for 167 us.
- Faster cold kernels would only help where the cold half shares SMs. The HBM-wait time it could hand to the HBM-light hot half is (7.34 - 5.72) x 16 = 26 us at p50.
- Using those 26 us needs an elastic hot half (a dynamic item queue plus a second grid after the cold half) and forced CTA placement. That is a co-scheduling design, not an engine change, and its static form is refuted (decode W6-D static SM splits x1.10-1.64).

(4) The best realistic cold-side stack is about -15..-30 us, i.e. +0.9-1.8% on the headline, below the bar:
- a fused persistent cold engine (one launch, one build_map, per-expert K1 -> K2 readiness counters, one fix-up round): -8..-15 us;
- lane Q (the T=256 cold half on v4cxs), already in flight: -3..-5 us;
- an untested wgmma-hot threshold of 32: 0..-15 us.

(5) The >= 45 us is in the hot half.
- At p50 its 7 experts take 142.4 us on the gate's own draws. That is 20.3 us per expert (10.6 el/clk/SM), against 7.34 us for a cold pass and K4's 12.6-18.2 el/clk/SM.
- The decode anatomies show 87.6-189.2 us for 4-9 hot experts at 1.20-1.73 TB/s, i.e. about 60-90 us of waste at p50.

claims_checked:
Each claim below is checked against moe CLAIMS.md and decode CLAIMS.md, newest line per mechanism.

Nothing proposed here reuses a refuted item:
- **Engine S cold** [refuted 10-27]: not proposed. Its reopen condition (P1 with 3-4 consumer WGs) did not clear: <= +3% (kstep §6).
- **wg2** [refuted, both forms] and **wg2 stream-K tail floor** [refuted]: not used.
- **K6 mixing** [node-only NO-GO]: not proposed. Co-residency of a hot and a cold CTA on one SM is the same physics and is also blocked by shared memory (204 KB + 113 KB) and registers (384 x 168). It is excluded.
- **S1a** [refuted]: consistent with this verdict's point (5) that the hot half's gap is fixed cost.
- **dq3 / dq4, k-slice, x-copy, X1-for-v4** [refuted], **repack F** [node-only, closed], **reuse r=2/4** [node-only, over the register cap]: these are the consumer levers already spent. This verdict says the consumer is not the T=256 bound, which agrees with them. eac sc0 caps any further scale-path trick at x1.12.
- **M03c cold-half knobs** [node-only, no pin]: consistent (cw7/9/11 and cold v3 lose; WG PDL off +0.39%).
- **Decode fork** [refuted] and **static SM splits x1.10-1.64** [decode CLAIMS:67]: this is why the co-scheduling route is left out (its static form is refuted; the elastic form is outside this angle).
- **v4x** [landed, classes 8/16/32/128] and **lane Q** (T=256 cold half on v4cxs, in flight): counted as -3..-5 us and not double-counted.
- **Marlin-hot H=-32 / -48** [superseded] and **H=-8** [refuted]: the -32 / -48 codes were Marlin-hot, and W5's H-20 was the wgx kernel. So a wgmma-hot threshold of 32 is untested, even though decode CLAIMS:57 says 'threshold sweep exhausted'. It is listed only as a cheap side item below the bar.
- **Hybrid at T=128** [refuted]: not touched.
- **K9 / T=1 items**: not relevant here.
decode_port:
The verdict is the same for decode.
- Decode's T=128/256 hybrid is serial (its fork is refuted: W6-F ee9142eb, decode CLAIMS:67), so cold-side cuts carry over 1:1.
- But decode's cold half is also HBM-bound: 2.86-3.26 TB/s and 7.34 us per pass across 9 judge anatomies.
- A fused cold engine's -8..-15 us on the v32 rows (437 / 710 us, sliding / full) and about -6..-10 us on the v16 rows is about +0.15-0.3% on the decode headline, below the bar.
- If it is ever built, it goes in hotcold_decode.py `_hc_experts`' cold launch (the same ea4 kernels), after eb-v4xd's T=128/256 cold routing (lane Q's decode port).
risks:
The verdict would be wrong in three cases:
- **(a) The H200 interleave differs from the node's.** On the judge, cold K1 is profiled at 136.7 us against about 90 us when it runs alone. So on the H200 the cold half shares SMs with the hot half and is partly consumer-bound. The rider's g198/g264 ratio settles this. Even then, the consumer has at most about x1.1-1.2 left (eac sc0 ceiling x1.12; P1 <= +3%), which is worth <= 10-15 us at p50.
- **(b) Most of the 27.4 us fixed term occupies SMs and can be removed.** The fused engine would then be worth about 20 us, still under 45.
- **(c) The out-of-angle co-schedule reaches its ideal of about 26 us.**

Even (a), (b) and (c) together reach about 45-50 us only if every piece hits its ideal (P about 0.05).

Side item for the main thread (cheap, below the bar):
- A wgmma-hot threshold of 32: a new H code with HM_WG_HOT threshold 32, so 17-32-route experts become two cold passes at about 13.5-14.7 us instead of about 20 us per hot expert.
- The prepare-time race decides it.
- It risks more cold HBM bytes in the fork and needs a measured per-expert hot cost by route count.

The real >= 45 us lever is the hot half: about 20 us per hot expert at 10.6 el/clk/SM, against K4's 12.6-18.2.

Nothing to dispatch: no check and no build. This is the reopen condition only.

One node run (gpunode06, moe-only, about 10 GPU-min, no code change): the nodejudge E3 nsys pass on the board bytes, verify 32, arms board and h16, with --gpu-metrics-devices=<gpu> --gpu-metrics-frequency=100000 added. Compute the idle SM-us per replay as the integral of (1 - SMs Active) over the span, times 132, and take the median over reps.
- Reopen the unified-schedule design only if the fork's median idle is at least 60 us-GPU per replay (at least 18% of the ~340 us node span), which puts the fluid potential at 45 us or more.
- Keep it closed at 40 us-GPU or less. That is my prediction: about 23 us of head/end plus about 10-15 us of half-SM head-of-line blocking.

Even after a reopen, the first judge rung would be a print-only prepare race of the unified kernel against H-16f at the p10/p50/p90 judge draws (read flush, 2 rounds), killed below x1.10 in any round.
spec:
NOT RECOMMENDED FOR A BUILD. Recorded so a reopen does not start from zero.

A) UFS, the unified fork-free schedule, T=256 only (the only design on this angle with a modeled ceiling near the bar).

Kernel shape:
- One persistent launch after wg_gather (PDL). Grid 132, 1 CTA/SM, wg_core's CTA: 384 threads, WG0 producer at setmaxnreg 40, WG1/WG2 consumers at 232.
- smem: wg's 4 x 41,984 B ring plus epilogue. Cold pieces reuse the ring as 3 stages of 53,504 B: two 18,432 B v4 records plus 16 x 1,040 B x rows. Ladder-2: at D=3 and 1 CTA/SM, v4 matches 2 CTAs/SM.

Prologue (every CTA, as v4x build_map_x): build the cold pass list from topk_ids, skipping experts with more than 16 routes, and the hot chunk table (wg_kernel's chunk scan).

Queues (atomic counters in a 16-int workspace, reset by a memset node):
- H13: hot w13 items (chunk, tile 0..63) in LPT bucket order (N128 first);
- H2: hot w2 items (chunk, tile 0..31), eligible once the chunk's H13 done-counter reaches 64;
- C1: cold K1 half-super-group pieces (pass, sg 0..63, kh 0..1, 4 units each);
- C2: cold K2 pieces (pass, sg 0..31, kh), eligible once the pass's C1 counter reaches 128.
- Dispatch, by thread 0 with an smem broadcast, in priority order: H2 ready, then H13, then C2 ready, then C1.

Bodies:
- Hot items run wg_core consume_item<NB,G> unchanged, so they stay bitwise.
- Cold pieces run v4x consume/consume2. Partials go to ws[(class, pass, sg, kh)] with one ticket per (pass, sg). The second arriver sums slot 0 + slot 1 in k order and runs the v4x epilogue (deterministic). Stamp a counter after each piece.
- Post-norm unchanged, after the kernel.

Race and checks: race as H-16u against H-16f at a 1.01 margin every round; canary, then a copy check.

Model: median row ~278 us (range 262-292), ceiling 264.

B) Shelf item, ACS (align-free cold start), below the bar, at -0 to -10 us (+0-0.5%):
- A v4x twin with a hot-skip threshold in pdl bits 9..13. build_map_x zeroes cnt[e] for experts with more than 16 routes and skips their pos_r entries.
- _hm_experts launches k13/k2 on the raw topk_ids with start = bank start, before the align, and captures align + gather + wg13 + wg2 on the fork stream ahead of K1.
- Race it against H-16f at 1.01 every round.

decode_port:
Decode runs serial H-16, pinned (the fork was refuted inside the layer). UFS would port as one kernel in decode's PDL chain, so it does not need the fork. Against serial the model gives x1.13-1.19 on the T=256 expert block, about 33-48 us per verify_32 row. At 0.0328 %/us that is decode +1.1-1.6%, also below the bar.

ACS ports trivially: run the cold half first on the raw topk_ids, then align → gather → wg → comb, with the align PDL-overlapped. That gives about 5-10 us per verify_32 row, about +0.2-0.3% decode.

Moe and decode can share one wg_core/ea4x source.
predicted_row_us: No build is recommended, so the row stays at 304.7 us. If UFS were built anyway: median ~278 us (range 262-292 across calibrations), zero-overhead ceiling ~264 us. The bar is 259.7 us. ACS alone: 295-305 us.
risks:
If UFS is built anyway:
1. One function holding both wgmma and mma.sync paths may get its wgmma serialized by ptxas (C7512).
2. K6-like interference when a CTA switches roles (ring drain, register pressure at setmaxnreg 232 for the mma.sync path).
3. Coarse hot items (17-29 us) set the tail if the LPT order or the dependencies stall.
4. Cold pieces are no longer bitwise-equal to v4's stream-K order. They are deterministic, but the copy check and canary need new tolerances.
5. Prepare time and size: a new module of about 25-30 KB.
6. The node cannot rank it, because node and judge flip on hybrid races (X0b).

The model's main uncertainty is the hot item cost calibration (scale 1.1-1.4), which moves the ceiling from -32 to -54 us. The nsys GPU-metrics run in gate_rung resolves it cheaply.

label: design:t256-2
title: No STRUCTURAL/BYTES design clears the verify_32 bar. The path already reads each expert once, overlap across SMs is zero-sum, and the structural slack totals about 15-35 us, short of the 45 us needed
mechanism:
VERDICT: headline 0. Nothing on this angle reaches -45 us at T=256 with a credible probability.

1) The bytes floor is already met. Each expert costs 28,311,552 B. At the judge's mean of 24.6 distinct local experts (backed out of SoL 108.9, which counts only 0.75 x distinct), that is 696.5 MB: 145 us at 4.8 TB/s and 159 us at the 4.37 TB/s ring. The current path reads every distinct expert exactly once:
- cold experts (<= 16 rows) get one 16-row pass each;
- hot experts get one wg chunk of up to 128 routes.
The only re-read is the busiest expert on the p10/p90 gate draws (155 / 143 rows), which splits into 2 chunks. That is 1.00-1.04x the read-once bytes. x, h and cache3 total under 10 MB and stay in L2. So no re-read, L2-reuse or expert-order lever exists. Lossless compression would add ALU work to kernels that are per-SM bound, so it would lose. The row (297.1 us, 787a2815) is 1.86x the ring floor. The gap is SM time, not bytes.

2) Where the 137 us above the floor sits, at the p50 gate draw:
- **Hot half:** about 147 us standalone for 7 experts, 1.35 TB/s, 21 us per expert. Decode's judge anatomy at T=256 reads the same 1.35 TB/s. The ring would take 45 us. This is the RS-wgmma K-step rate (13-20 el/clk/SM at N=64-128) plus item imbalance.
- **Cold half:** 145 us = 27.4 + 7.34 x 16, at 88% of the ring.
- **Glue on the critical path:** align 10.1 + post-norm 5.7 = 15.8 us.
- **Fork:** it already recovers 10-21 us (x1.031-1.066).

3) The structural levers, each measured or bounded:
- **Concurrency or SM partition: zero-sum.** On the node, a balanced partition (g132) read x0.99 and skewed ones read x0.78 / x0.62. On the judge, the priority -1 fork serialized (x0.997-1.004).
- **Mixing hot and cold roles in one CTA:** K6 NO-GO. Even its best mixed/(hot+cold) of 0.83 would be at most -17% of the expert span, as a whole new engine.
- **Expert-major persistent / unified dynamic queue:** it can only recover scheduling slack. That slack is about 21 us on the node (331 us span vs 310 us of summed per-SM active cycles). On the judge it is unmeasured: about 17-43 us beyond what the fork already takes.
- **Hot item balance:** the static stride has max/avg x1.26 (w13) and x1.42 (w2) in the model; the node's ncu reads x1.19 / x1.43. Greedy LPT gets both to x1.11, about -14 us of hot makespan, which the fork partly absorbs.
- **Fast CUDA align:** 10.1 -> ~3 us, so -7.
- **PDL post-norm:** -2.
- **Chunk cap 256 for the busiest expert:** 0 to -5, on the p10/p90 draws only.
- **Fusing gate/up/down per expert:** the w13 -> w2 boundary idle is already filled by the other half, so 3-5 us at most.

The credible stack is -15 to -35 us, which is +0.9 to +2.1% on the headline. The bar is -45 us (252.1 us, +2.78%). P(>= 45) is about 0.1, so gain x p is about 0.3%, far below the 1.5% bar.

The remaining gap to the bytes floor is the hot kernel's per-SM K-step (dequant -> 8 wgmma -> wait<0> per stage). That is the hot-kernel-internals line, which CLAIMS marks exhausted (W5 wgx, wg2, S1a, ping-pong). It is not a structural or bytes lever.

Decision:

spec:
None of this is a build for tonight (the user's 23:22Z steer: in-flight work only). These are shelf riders, each below the bar, in case a lead needs a stack.

**R1. Fast align (moe T=256 and decode T=128/256): about -7 us per row, bitwise.**
- Replace `_hm_align_kernel` (Triton, grid count+1) with one CUDA CTA of 1024 threads:
  1. Each thread loads 2 of the 2048 ids and computes the local id as (id - ls) mod 256 < count.
  2. Count per expert with smem atomics.
  3. Warp 0 does the 32-bin hot/cold classification (> HOT rows), the padding to 16 and the exclusive prefix.
  4. Compute stable ascending ranks: per-warp `__match_any_sync` + popc gives the rank inside the warp; a [32 warps][32 experts] smem table, scanned per expert, gives each warp's base.
  5. Write sc / bc / sh / bh / nc / nh / local_ids / cold_ids with exactly `_hm_align_ref`'s layout: sentinel n in the padding and past the used length, and -1 in unused blocks.
- Gate: `_hm_align_cmp` exact equality over the canary routings plus 64 random and skewed draws. Any mismatch keeps the Triton kernel.
- Race: the row graph read-flushed, every draw >= 1.005.

**R2. Hot-half dynamic LPT claim: model -7 / -7 us on hot w13 / w2 makespan; fork absorbs part, so -5..-12 us on the moe row. Bitwise.**
- In wg_kernel, the producer thread replaces `it += gridDim.x` with `it = atomicAdd(&ctr[G], 1)` over an order that is sorted by bucket descending, expert, tile, then chunk. The prologue builds this order in smem from s_cnb.
- The producer passes each claimed item to the consumers through a 4-deep smem slot ring guarded by an mbarrier. A sentinel ends the loop.
- The counter resets inside the kernel: the last-exiting CTA zeroes it, using an exit ticket with acq_rel.
- No arithmetic changes per item, so the outputs are bitwise identical to wg. The canary checks equality with the incumbent on 12 routings, with NaN-poisoned h_sorted / cache3.

**R3 (optional). Cold K2 at T=256: whole-record dynamic claim.**
- Use 16 rows x full K per unit, with no stream-K fix-up (no reduction across CTAs). It absorbs the staggered starts after the hot half.
- It is not bitwise with v4cxs (different fp32 order), so it needs the fp32 canary at half the bound.

Race each rider separately (one routable novelty per check).
risks:
- **Risk to the verdict itself:** the judge's scheduling slack after the fork could be larger than the node's 21 us. An inference from the judge's standalone halves (hot ~147, cold ~145, summed per-SM active ~229-240, span ~281) allows 38-53 us, and the fork already takes 10-21 of it. If DIAG-SLACK256 reads >= 35 us, a unified dynamic-claim engine plus R1 could reach -45 us. That is the one way this angle reopens.
- **Riders:**
  - R2 can lose if the extra producer -> consumer hand-off per item costs more than the imbalance saves. Items are 10-21 us long, so the hand-off is under 0.5%.
  - R2's counter needs a reset every call; a graph-safe exit ticket is the precedent from v4x.
  - R1 must match the reference layout exactly.
  - At moe T=256, the fork absorbs part of the hot tail, so R2's realized gain is uncertain (-5..-12 us).
- **Below the bar on purpose:** the full credible stack R1-R3 is -15 to -35 us, which is +0.9 to +2.1% on the headline.
